rules: Anyone paid, given the product free or at a discount, or with a family or business tie to you has to say so, even if they think their review is fair.
The disclosure goes with the post itself, not only in the profile or bio.
In a video, say it in the video, out loud and on screen, not only in the caption.
Plain words work: ad, advertisement or sponsored. Vague tags like sp, spon or collab do not.
Don't bury it in a pile of hashtags or links.
The platform's paid partnership label helps, but use it on top of their own disclosure, not instead of it.
On a live stream, repeat it now and then for people who join late.

tiktok.name: Spark Ads video code
creatorSteps: In the TikTok app, make sure ad authorization is allowed for the account (Settings and privacy, or Creator tools).
Open the video, tap the three dots, then Ad settings.
Agree to the advertising terms if asked, and turn on Ad authorization.
Generate a video code and pick how long it lasts: 7, 30, 60 or 365 days.
Tap Copy code and send it to the business.
advertiserSteps: In TikTok Ads Manager, go to Tools, then Creative library.
Click Spark ads posts, then Apply for authorization.
Paste the video code, click Search, and confirm it's the right video.
notes: The caption can't be edited once the post is authorized as an ad.
A private video becomes public once it's used in a campaign.

meta.note: On Instagram and Facebook, a creator's post can run as a partnership ad from their handle only with their permission: a partnership ad code for one post, or account-level permission. They can withdraw it at any time. Meta's menus change, so follow the steps in Meta's help center when you set it up.
